say.en: Two programs both sort 10 numbers in a blink. With a million numbers one takes a second and the other a week. Big O notation predicts this before you run anything. In this lesson: Define time complexity and Big O notation.
Find the Big O of loops, nested loops and halving loops.

body.en: The time complexity of an algorithm describes how the number of basic operations grows with the input size n. *Big O notation* gives an upper bound on this growth for large n, keeping only the dominant term and ignoring constant factors: 3n² + 5n + 2 is O(n²). Common classes, from fastest to slowest growth: O(1) constant, O(log n) logarithmic, O(n) linear, O(n log n), O(n²) quadratic, O(n³) cubic, O(2^n) exponential.

body.en: The running time can depend on the data, not only on n. Linear search: best case O(1) (the key is first), worst case O(n) (last or absent), *average* about n/2 comparisons, which is still O(n). Binary search: O(1) best, O(log n) worst. Bubble sort with the early-exit check: O(n) best (already sorted), O(n²) worst. Selection sort: O(n²) in every case. Big O is normally quoted for the worst case, which gives a guarantee.
